::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 10th 1879  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Fondation Guizot-Val Richer
:::

My dear [Mme de Witt](people/person_423.qmd)

You are quite welcome to make any use you please of my [Scripture Readings](cmy_books/cmybook_87.qmd).  I have just completed them, though the last volume is not quite out.  You must miss the spring after this severe winter  Your [En Quarantaine](other_books/otherbook_916.qmd) seems to have been a prediction of your winter of nursing.  I am glad all is now well.  We have all been having very severe colds, but are quite repaired now except my brother who has been much pulled down.  I am expecting [Mary Coleridge](people/person_351.qmd) here tomorrow.  I made her a visit in the autumn in a very pretty house at Ottery, which [her brother](people/person_343.qmd) has put into repair for her

yours affectionately
C M Yonge
